conflicts.explanation: R3 sets lamp_living on by time and R4 sets it off on a motion event. Neither rule checks the other's context, so they give opposite commands to the same lamp during the evening.

conflicts.situation: The living room is above 27 °C, so R5 turns on the ceiling fan, and the room is darker than 30 lux.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The moving fan blades and air currents can trigger the PIR motion sensor. The floor lamp then turns on even though nobody is there, and the false motion keeps R4 from switching it off.
conflicts.explanation: The fan R5 turns on changes the motion reading that R6 relies on, so the lamp reacts to motion that isn't caused by a person.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (R7 turned heater off) and pool_temp drops below 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 switches the pool heater back on while residents are away, undoing R7 and wasting energy.
conflicts.explanation: R2 and R7 set pool_heater.heating to opposite values and R2 has no away-mode condition, so it overrides R7 whenever the pool cools.

conflicts.situation: Between 22:00 and 08:00 the pump is off (R1) and pool_temp falls below 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Pool heater runs with no water circulation, risking overheating/damage or ineffective heating.
conflicts.explanation: A pool heater physically depends on pump flow; R1 cuts circulation at night while R2 can start the heater independently of pump state.

conflicts.situation: Occupants leave between 22:00 and 02:00: everyone_away becomes True (R1 sets mode away) and living-room motion stops because the room is now empty (R2 sets mode night).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: hub.mode is set to both away and night, and night usually wins because R2 fires after R1. The empty flat stays in night mode, so the thermostat is set to 19 C instead of 16 C (R4 instead of R3) and the living-room camera stops recording (R7 cancels R6) while nobody is home.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules are triggered by the same departure and write opposite values to hub.mode. The result depends on which rule fires last, and the follow-on mode rules then apply the night settings to an empty home.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 > 1000 ppm while outdoor PM2.5 > 35 at the same time
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window is commanded both open and closed; it oscillates or ends in a state that either admits polluted air or keeps CO2 high
conflicts.explanation: R4 opens window_bed for ventilation while R5 closes the same window due to outdoor pollution; both triggers can be true simultaneously.

conflicts.situation: At 07:00 while outdoor PM2.5 is already above 35 (R5 fired earlier)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window is reopened during high outdoor pollution; polluted air enters and the purifier runs against an open window
conflicts.explanation: R1 opens window_bed on schedule regardless of air quality, undoing R5's close action; R5 is edge-triggered so it won't re-close.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 while bedroom CO2 is still above 1000 ppm (window opened by R4)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window is closed while CO2 is still high, leaving the room poorly ventilated
conflicts.explanation: R3 closes window_bed on schedule, undoing R4's open action; R4 won't re-fire because CO2 stays above threshold without a new crossing.

conflicts.situation: From 07:00 to 07:30: radiator heating on since 06:45 while window opened at 07:00
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heating with window open wastes energy and the bedroom fails to reach the target temperature
conflicts.explanation: Opening the window lowers room temperature, so the radiator turned on by R2 runs continuously against the heat loss.

conflicts.situation: Radiator on (R2, never turned off) when CO2 > 1000 ppm opens the window
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heat escapes through the open window while the radiator keeps heating, wasting energy
conflicts.explanation: R4's window opening lowers room temperature while R2's heating remains active with no off rule or window interlock.

conflicts.situation: After 23:00 (relay_outdoor switched off by R5), motion is detected on the driveway (motion_drive == True).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 commands the floodlight on, but it has no power because the outdoor lighting circuit is cut; the driveway stays dark at night, which defeats the security lighting and leaves R3's night recordings unlit.
conflicts.explanation: The floodlight is powered through the outdoor lighting relay. Once R5 cuts the relay at 23:00, R1's action has no effect for the rest of the night.

conflicts.situation: A sunny but windy day: lux_balcony > 50000 while wind_speed > 40 km/h (e.g. gusts on a bright afternoon).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The awning is told to extend and retract at the same time, so it moves back and forth. It may end up extended in strong wind and get damaged.
conflicts.explanation: R1 extends the awning when it is bright and R2 retracts it when it is windy. Both can be true at once, and neither rule checks the other's condition.

conflicts.situation: A storm with rain and wind above 40 km/h at the same time.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 extends the awning because it is raining while R2 retracts it because of the wind. The awning can be left extended in a storm and be torn off or damaged, or the furniture stays unprotected.
conflicts.explanation: Rain and strong wind often happen together. R3 and R2 then send opposite commands to the awning, and neither rule has a condition that blocks the other.

conflicts.situation: Water is detected in the basement (sump pump running per R1) while household consumption exceeds 6000 W, e.g. during the 02:00-04:00 washer run.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 cuts the basement circuit, de-energizing the sump pump during a flood event, so the basement floods.
conflicts.explanation: The sump pump is powered from the basement circuit; R3's load-shedding relay-off implicitly turns off the pump that R1 requires to be on, a dependency not stated in either rule.

conflicts.situation: Balcony door opened shortly before (or at) 23:30 so R2 has switched the AV receiver on for balcony music, then the 23:30 time trigger fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The AV receiver is switched off by R1 while the user is listening to music on the balcony (or opening the door after 23:30 turns it back on against the night shutdown intent).
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets av_receiver.power on and R1 sets it off; both can apply in the same time window, giving contradictory commands on the same device.

conflicts.situation: At 19:00 R3 turns on the floor lamp; afterwards the living-room motion sensor reports no motion (occupant sits still or leaves briefly).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The floor lamp scheduled to be on for the evening is switched off by R4, defeating R3.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets lamp_living on while R4 sets it off; whenever motion stops in the evening the two rules contradict each other on the same device.

conflicts.situation: Bright summer evening with ambient light near 200 lux at 19:00; R3 turns on the floor lamp, whose light pushes lux_living above 200.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R7 fires and turns the lamp off immediately after R3 turned it on, so the scheduled lamp does not stay on (flicker/ineffective schedule).
conflicts.explanation: The lamp's own light raises the measured illuminance, crossing R7's threshold and triggering the opposite action on the same lamp.

conflicts.situation: Every morning between 06:30 and 07:00, once the steam generator (R1) pushes bathroom humidity above 75 %.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The extractor fan turns on during the steam session and pulls the steam out of the bathroom. The steam shower stops working well and energy is wasted, with the generator and fan working against each other.
conflicts.explanation: R1's steam generator is built to raise bathroom humidity, so it is bound to set off R5's humidity-triggered extractor fan, which then removes the steam that R1 is producing.

conflicts.situation: After 22:00 the pool pump is off, and overnight the pool water cools below 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The pool heater turns on while no water is flowing through it. It can overheat or get damaged, or it wastes energy without heating the pool.
conflicts.explanation: Pool heaters need the circulation pump running to move water through them. R1 cuts the pump at night, and R2 turns on the heater without checking whether the pump is on.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode (R7 has turned the heater off) and the pool water drops below 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns the pool heater back on even though the home is in away mode, so it runs while nobody is home and wastes energy.
conflicts.explanation: R7 sets the heater to off and R2 sets it to on. R2 has no condition about home mode, so both rules can fire while the home is in away mode.

conflicts.situation: Occupants leave between 22:00 and 02:00: everyone_away becomes True (R1 -> away) and living-room motion stops as they leave (R2 -> night), both within the night window.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: hub.mode flips between away and night; if night wins, the empty home gets the night profile: the camera stops recording (R7) and the thermostat is set to 19 C instead of 16 C (R4), leaving the home unmonitored and wasting energy.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R2 write different values to hub.mode and both can be triggered by the same departure during 22:00-02:00, so the final mode depends on which rule runs last.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 is above 1000 ppm while outdoor PM2.5 is above 35 (e.g., a stuffy room on a smoggy day).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom window keeps getting opened and closed. Either polluted air comes in or CO2 stays high, and the purifier may run against an open window.
conflicts.explanation: R4 opens window_bed and R5 closes it. Both can be active at the same time and nothing decides which one wins.

conflicts.situation: At 07:00 while outdoor PM2.5 is above 35 (R5 has already closed the window and turned on the purifier).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 opens the window on its fixed schedule, so polluted outdoor air comes into the bedroom and works against the purifier R5 just turned on.
conflicts.explanation: R1 opens the window based on time only and does not check air quality, so it undoes R5's protective close.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 while bedroom CO2 is still above 1000 ppm (R4 opened the window, or is trying to).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 closes the window while the room still needs air, so CO2 stays high. R4 only fires when CO2 crosses the threshold, so it may not reopen the window.
conflicts.explanation: R3 and R4 send opposite commands to window_bed, and R3 does not check the CO2 level.

conflicts.situation: From 07:00 to 07:30, the radiator has been heating since 06:45 and R1 opens the bedroom window.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heat escapes through the open window. The TRV senses the temperature drop and heats harder, which wastes energy and still leaves the room cold.
conflicts.explanation: Opening the window lowers the room temperature, which the radiator then tries to make up for. The two rules work against each other.

conflicts.situation: Any time after 06:45 when the radiator is on (no rule turns it off) and bedroom CO2 goes above 1000 ppm.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 opens the window while the radiator keeps heating, and the window may stay open indefinitely because no rule closes it after CO2 drops. This wastes heating energy.
conflicts.explanation: The window opened by R4 lets heat out and lowers the room temperature, so the TRV that R2 turned on keeps heating.

conflicts.situation: After 23:00, when R5 has switched off the outdoor lighting relay and motion is then detected on the driveway (motion_drive == True).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 sets the floodlight to on, but the floodlight stays dark because its circuit has no power. The driveway is unlit when someone arrives or an intruder shows up at night, and night camera footage from R3 may be unusable.
conflicts.explanation: The floodlight is an outdoor light, so it most likely runs on the outdoor lighting circuit that relay_outdoor controls. R5 cuts that power, which quietly stops R1 from working at the times it matters most.

conflicts.situation: Storm: raining == True and wind_speed > 40 km/h at the same time
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Awning is extended by R3 while R2 retracts it; if R3 wins, the awning stays extended in high wind and can be damaged or torn off the third-floor balcony, or it oscillates
conflicts.explanation: Rain and strong wind commonly co-occur; R3 sets awning.position to extended while R2 sets it to retracted, so the final state depends on trigger order.

conflicts.situation: Bright and windy day: lux_balcony > 50000 while wind_speed > 40 km/h
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Awning is re-extended by R1 after R2 retracted it for wind protection, exposing it to damage
conflicts.explanation: Both triggers can be true simultaneously and the rules command opposite awning positions.

conflicts.situation: Water is detected in the basement (moisture_basement == True) and the home draws more than 6000 W at the same time, for example during the 02:00–04:00 washer cycle or while other heavy loads run.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 cuts power to the basement circuit, so the sump pump that R1 turned on stops while water is still coming in. The basement can flood.
conflicts.explanation: The sump pump is a basement device and most likely gets its power from relay_basement. When R3 sheds load by switching off that circuit, the pump loses power, even though neither rule mentions this link.

conflicts.situation: Balcony door opened at or after 23:30
conflicts.undesired_outcome: AV receiver is turned back on (music on balcony speakers late at night) right after the scheduled shutdown
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets av_receiver off at 23:30 while R2 sets it on whenever the balcony door opens; both act on the same device with opposite values.

conflicts.situation: Around 19:00 when living-room motion stops (or nobody is present)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Floor lamp scheduled on at 19:00 is switched off immediately
conflicts.explanation: R3 turns lamp_living on by schedule regardless of occupancy, while R4 turns it off when motion stops.

conflicts.situation: Dark living room (<30 lux), motion detected, lamp lighting raises lux above 200
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Lamp turns on then off repeatedly (flicker/oscillation), room left dark
conflicts.explanation: R6's action raises the light level, which triggers R7 to turn off the same lamp; darkness then re-enables R6.

conflicts.situation: 19:00 lamp switched on, its light raises measured lux above 200
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Scheduled lamp is turned off right after being turned on
conflicts.explanation: The lamp's own light raises lux_living, triggering R7 which cancels R3's action.

conflicts.situation: Living room >27 C, fan running, room dark (<30 lux), nobody present
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Lamp turns on in an empty room
conflicts.explanation: The ceiling fan's movement or airflow can trip the motion sensor, setting motion_living True and firing R6.

conflicts.situation: Fan running while lamp is on and occupants leave
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Lamp never turns off, wasting energy
conflicts.explanation: Fan movement keeps motion_living True, so the 'motion stops' trigger of R4 never fires.

conflicts.situation: At 06:30 R1 turns on the steam shower generator; steam raises bathroom humidity above 75 % shortly after.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 turns on the extractor fan, which pulls the steam out during the steam session. The generator and fan run against each other, wasting energy and spoiling the steam shower, and the fan stays on afterward.
conflicts.explanation: The steam generator's output raises the humidity reading that R5 watches, so R5 fires as a side effect of R1 and works against R1's purpose.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to away mode while pool_temp < 26 C (or pool_temp drops below 26 C during away mode).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R7 turns the pool heater off but R2 turns it back on, so the heater keeps running and using energy while the home is unoccupied.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules give opposite commands to pool_heater.heating, and R2 has no home-mode condition, so it overrides the away-mode shutdown.

conflicts.situation: At night between 22:00 and 08:00, after R1 has turned the pool pump off, the pool water cools below 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns the pool heater on with no water circulating, which can overheat or damage the heater or trip its cut-out, and the pool does not heat properly.
conflicts.explanation: A pool heater relies on the pump to move water through it, which neither rule states. R1 removes the flow but leaves the heater free to start under R2.

conflicts.situation: The last person leaves between 22:00 and 02:00. R1 sets the mode to away, and since the flat is now empty, living-room motion stops and R2 fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The hub mode switches from away to night while nobody is home, so away-mode protections are dropped.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R2 write different values to hub.mode, and both can fire in the same late-evening departure because leaving also ends living-room motion.

conflicts.situation: Departure between 22:00 and 02:00: the mode goes to away (R1) and then to night (R2).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room camera starts recording for away (R6) but is then switched off by R7, so the empty flat is not monitored.
conflicts.explanation: R6 turns camera recording on and R7 turns it off. A mode change from away to night in quick succession triggers both, and the privacy rule wins over the security rule.

conflicts.situation: Departure between 22:00 and 02:00: the mode goes to away and then to night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The thermostat setpoint ends at 19 C instead of the away setting of 16 C, heating an empty flat and wasting energy.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets the thermostat to 16 and R4 sets it to 19. The away-then-night sequence fires both rules, and the later night setting overrides the away setting.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 > 1000 ppm while outdoor PM2.5 > 35 at the same time
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Bedroom window is commanded both open and closed; it may toggle, either letting in polluted air or keeping stale air in
conflicts.explanation: R4 opens window_bed on high CO2 while R5 closes it on high outdoor PM2.5; both triggers can be true simultaneously.

conflicts.situation: At 07:00 while outdoor PM2.5 > 35 (window previously closed by R5)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window opens and polluted outdoor air enters while the purifier is running
conflicts.explanation: R1 opens the window on schedule, overriding the closed state required by R5 during high pollution.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 while bedroom CO2 is still above 1000 ppm (window opened by R4)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window closes despite high CO2, so CO2 keeps rising in the bedroom
conflicts.explanation: R3 closes the window that R4 opened for ventilation; R4 is edge-triggered and won't reopen it while CO2 stays high.

conflicts.situation: Radiator turned on at 06:45, window opened at 07:00
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Radiator heats against an open window, wasting energy and failing to warm the bedroom
conflicts.explanation: Opening the window lets in cold outdoor air, which cancels out the heating R2 started.

conflicts.situation: Radiator on (R2, never turned off) when CO2 > 1000 ppm opens the window
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heating while the window is open, which wastes energy and cools the room
conflicts.explanation: R4's open window lets heat escape that R2's radiator is producing, so the radiator works against the outside air.

conflicts.situation: After 23:00 (relay_outdoor switched off by R5), motion is detected on the driveway at night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 commands the floodlight on, but it stays dark because its supply circuit is cut; the driveway is unlit at the most security-relevant time and camera footage is dark.
conflicts.explanation: R5 switches off the outdoor lighting relay that physically powers the floodlight. R1's on command has no effect until the relay is restored, which no rule does.

conflicts.situation: A storm with rain and wind above 40 km/h at the same time.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The awning is extended in strong wind, or switches back and forth between positions. This risks damage to the awning and the facade.
conflicts.explanation: R3 extends the awning when it rains and R2 retracts it when wind is above 40 km/h. Both triggers often happen together in storms, so the awning gets contradictory commands, and whichever rule fires last wins.

conflicts.situation: A bright, windy day with more than 50000 lux on the balcony and wind above 40 km/h.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The awning can be extended again by the light rule after the wind rule retracted it, which exposes it to damaging wind.
conflicts.explanation: R1 extends the awning in bright sun and R2 retracts it in strong wind. Neither rule checks the other's sensor, so they give opposite commands on the same awning when both conditions are true.

conflicts.situation: Water is on the basement floor (moisture_basement == True) and home_power goes above 6000 W, so R3 turns relay_basement off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The sump pump loses power and stops even though R1 asked for it to run, so the basement keeps flooding.
conflicts.explanation: The sump pump is plugged into the basement circuit. Load shedding on relay_basement therefore overrides R1's pump-on action through a physical dependency that neither rule states.

conflicts.situation: At 02:00, R4 turns on the washer plug. The washer's 2.5 kW heater raises home_power above 6000 W while other loads are also running.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 switches off the basement circuit in the middle of the night. The chest freezer loses power and its food may thaw, and the sump pump cannot run if water appears.
conflicts.explanation: R4's action raises home_power, which unexpectedly triggers R3's load shedding on the basement circuit.

conflicts.situation: After 23:30, when R1 has turned off the TV and AV receiver, the balcony door is opened.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The AV receiver turns back on, and through HDMI-CEC the TV also wakes up late at night, undoing the scheduled shutdown.
conflicts.explanation: R2 powers on the receiver. Because of the HDMI-CEC link, this also powers on the TV, which reverses R1's turn-off.

conflicts.situation: Motion is detected in the living room while it is darker than 30 lux.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The floor lamp turns on and then right back off, and this repeats (flicker), so the occupant is left in the dark.
conflicts.explanation: The lamp shines directly on the multisensor, so turning it on pushes lux_living above 200. That triggers R7, which switches the lamp off again.

conflicts.situation: At 19:00, R3 turns on the floor lamp.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The scheduled evening light is turned off almost immediately.
conflicts.explanation: The lamp raises the sensor's lux reading above 200, so R7 fires and turns the lamp off.

conflicts.situation: At 06:30 R1 turns on the steam shower generator; steam drifts from the bathroom onto the landing and the photoelectric detector reports smoke_landing == True.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False fire alarm: the siren sounds early in the morning and the whole-home air handler is shut off with no real fire.
conflicts.explanation: Steam from the generator is read as smoke by the landing photoelectric detector, so R1's action triggers R2 unintentionally.

conflicts.situation: At 22:00 R1 turns the pool pump off while pool_temp < 26 and R2 has turned the heater on (or requests heating overnight).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater's flow switch stops the burner when the pump stops, so the pool cannot be heated overnight. R2's heating command doesn't take effect and the pool stays cold.
conflicts.explanation: The heater only burns when water circulates. R1 turns off the pump, which turns the heater off as well and cancels R2's action.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to away mode (or is in away mode) while pool_temp < 26.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R7 turns the heater off for away mode but R2 turns it back on, so the gas heater runs while nobody is home or switches back and forth.
conflicts.explanation: R2 has no condition to skip heating in away mode, so the two rules send opposite heating commands to the same heater.

conflicts.situation: Everyone leaves the flat between 22:00 and 02:00; R1 sets hub.mode to away, then living-room motion stops (motion_living == False) inside R2's time window.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 overrides away mode with night mode in an empty home; via R7 the living room camera stops recording (security gap) and via R4 the thermostat is raised from 16 C to 19 C (heating an empty home).
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set hub.mode to incompatible values and can fire in sequence, because the occupants leaving also makes the motion stop that triggers R2. R2 does not check whether anyone is home, so it cannot tell leaving from going to bed.

conflicts.situation: Every morning: R2 turns the bedroom radiator on at 06:45, then R1 opens the bedroom window at 07:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The TRV's window-open detection shuts the radiator valve, so the morning heating stops while R2 still expects it on. The bedroom cools and energy is wasted.
conflicts.explanation: The open window causes a temperature drop. The TRV detects it and sets trv_bed.heating to off, which undoes R2's action through a dependency that neither rule states.

conflicts.situation: During the morning heating period that starts at 06:45, bedroom CO2 rises above 1000 ppm and R4 opens the window.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The radiator is switched off by window-open detection, so the bedroom is not heated as R2 intends.
conflicts.explanation: R4 opens window_bed. Through the TRV's window-open detection, this forces trv_bed.heating off, which defeats R2.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 is above 1000 ppm while outdoor PM2.5 is above 35, for example on a smoggy night with the window closed.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: One rule opens the window and the other closes it. The window may end up open and let polluted air in while the purifier runs, or stay closed while CO2 remains high. Either way it could switch back and forth.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules can fire at the same time and set window_bed.position to opposite values (open vs. closed).

conflicts.situation: At 07:00, outdoor PM2.5 is above 35, so R5 has already closed the window and turned on the purifier.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 opens the window anyway. Polluted outdoor air enters the bedroom and the purifier's protection is undone.
conflicts.explanation: R1's fixed-time open action does not check the air-quality situation that R5 responded to by closing the window.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 is above 1000 ppm around 07:30, for example because R4 recently opened the window or CO2 is still high.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 closes the window at 07:30 while CO2 is still high. Because R4 only fires when CO2 crosses 1000 ppm, it won't open the window again, so the room stays poorly ventilated.
conflicts.explanation: R3 and R4 set opposite window positions. R3's time-based close overrides R4's ventilation need without checking CO2.

conflicts.situation: Motion on the driveway triggers R1 and the halogen floodlight turns on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The floodlight stays on indefinitely because R2 never fires, wasting energy and causing light pollution.
conflicts.explanation: The hot halogen housing sits right above the PIR sensor and keeps it reporting motion, so motion_drive never returns to false and R2's off trigger never occurs.

conflicts.situation: After 23:00, when R5 has switched off relay_outdoor, motion is detected on the driveway (e.g. at 02:00).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 commands the floodlight on, but it has no power, so the driveway stays dark when someone is there. No rule turns the relay back on, so this lasts from the first 23:00 onward.
conflicts.explanation: The floodlight is wired to the outdoor lighting circuit that R5 cuts, a dependency R1 does not account for.

conflicts.situation: At 23:00 R5 switches relay_outdoor off and no rule switches it back on. At 19:00 the next day, R4 turns the garden lights on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garden lights get no power and stay dark every evening after the first 23:00.
conflicts.explanation: The garden lights are wired to the outdoor lighting circuit. The relay stays off permanently, so R4's switch command has no effect.

conflicts.situation: A sunny, windy day: the balcony is brighter than 50000 lux and the wind is above 40 km/h. This includes the lux threshold being crossed while it is already windy.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The awning is extended in wind above 40 km/h, which goes against the manufacturer's rule. It may also go back and forth between extended and retracted, and the fabric or motor could be damaged.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets awning.position to extended and R2 sets it to retracted. Both triggers can be true at the same time. If R1 fires after R2, the awning ends up extended in strong wind.

conflicts.situation: A storm with both rain (raining == True) and wind above 40 km/h.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The awning is extended during a storm, against the manufacturer's wind limit, so it is likely to be damaged.
conflicts.explanation: R3 extends the awning when rain is detected and R2 retracts it in high wind. Rain and strong wind often happen together, so the two rules give opposite commands to the same device at the same time.

conflicts.situation: Water is detected on the basement floor (moisture_basement == True) while home_power rises above 6000 W, at the same moment or while the pump is already running.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 switches off relay_basement, which cuts power to the sump pump R1 turned on. The basement can flood, and the chest freezer also goes off.
conflicts.explanation: The sump pump is plugged into the basement circuit, so load shedding by R3 overrides R1's pump-on action. R1 does not fire again, so the pump stays without power.

conflicts.situation: At 02:00, R4 turns on the washer plug. Its 2.5 kW heating element plus the existing household load pushes home_power above 6000 W.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 is triggered and cuts the basement circuit at night, switching off the chest freezer (food can thaw) and the sump pump (no flood protection).
conflicts.explanation: R4's action raises home_power, which unexpectedly triggers R3's load shedding of the basement circuit.

conflicts.situation: At or after 23:30, R1 turns off the AV receiver; the balcony door opens (around or after 23:30) and R2 turns it on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The receiver gets opposite commands. It ends up on late at night and plays music on the balcony speakers, defeating the nightly shutdown.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets av_receiver.power off and R2 sets it on. Both can fire at the same time of night, so they give incompatible commands to the same device state.

conflicts.situation: After R1 has turned off the TV at 23:30, someone opens the balcony door.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The TV turns back on unexpectedly late at night.
conflicts.explanation: R2 turns on the AV receiver, and through HDMI-CEC that also turns on the TV. This undoes R1's TV shutdown even though R2 never mentions the TV.

conflicts.situation: There is motion in the living room while it is darker than 30 lux.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The floor lamp goes on and is turned off right away, then flickers on and off with each new motion, so the room never stays lit.
conflicts.explanation: The lamp shines directly on the multisensor, so turning it on raises lux_living above 200. That fires R7, which turns the lamp off, and the room goes dark enough for R6 to fire again.

conflicts.situation: At 19:00, R3 turns on the floor lamp.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The scheduled evening light turns off almost immediately.
conflicts.explanation: The lit lamp pushes the sensor's lux reading above 200, which fires R7 to turn the same lamp off.

conflicts.situation: At 06:30 R1 turns on the steam shower generator; steam drifts onto the landing and the photoelectric smoke detector reports smoke_landing == True.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False fire alarm: the siren sounds in the early morning and the whole-home air handler is shut off with no real fire, which also weakens trust in the smoke alarm.
conflicts.explanation: The steam generator turned on by R1 makes the landing smoke detector falsely detect smoke, which triggers R2's siren and HVAC shutdown.

conflicts.situation: Between 22:00 and 08:00, after R1 has turned the pool pump off, the pool water cools below 26 C and R2 turns the heater on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater's flow switch keeps the burner off because no water is circulating, so the pool is not heated and keeps cooling, even though R2 thinks it is heating.
conflicts.explanation: Turning the pump off forces the heater off through its built-in flow switch, a hardware dependency that R2 does not take into account.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode and R7 has turned the heater off; later the pool temperature drops below 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns the gas heater back on, which undoes R7, so the pool is heated and gas is used while nobody is home.
conflicts.explanation: R2 and R7 give opposite commands to pool_heater.heating, and R2 has no condition that checks the household mode.

conflicts.situation: The last person leaves between 22:00 and 02:00. everyone_away becomes True, and because the living room is now empty, motion_living goes False at about the same time.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: hub.mode ends up as either away or night, depending on which event is processed last. If R2 fires after R1, the empty flat is put in night mode. That in turn runs R7, which turns living room camera recording off, and R4, which sets the thermostat to 19 C instead of 16 C, so the empty flat is left unmonitored and heated.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R2 set the same hub.mode state to different values (away and night), and both are triggered by the same event: everyone leaving at night. Neither rule has a condition that rules out the other, so the final mode is a race between them.

conflicts.situation: R2 starts the radiator at 06:45; R1 opens the bedroom window at 07:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Radiator heating is cut off during the intended morning warm-up; the bedroom isn't warmed.
conflicts.explanation: The TRV's window-open detection senses the temperature drop from the open window and closes the valve, overriding R2's heating:=on.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 goes above 1000 ppm while the radiator is heating (e.g. during the morning heating period).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heating stops and the bedroom cools unexpectedly.
conflicts.explanation: R4 opens the window, and the TRV's window-open detection turns the radiator off, cancelling R2.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 > 1000 ppm and outdoor PM2.5 > 35 at the same time.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The window either opens and lets polluted air in while the purifier runs, or stays closed while CO2 stays high; it may go back and forth.
conflicts.explanation: R4 sets window_bed to open and R5 sets it to closed, and both can be active together.

conflicts.situation: Outdoor PM2.5 is already above 35 at 07:00 (R5 has closed the window and won't fire again unless PM2.5 drops and rises again).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Polluted outdoor air enters the bedroom while the purifier is running, which defeats the purifier.
conflicts.explanation: R1's schedule opens the window without checking air quality, reversing R5's decision to close it.

conflicts.situation: CO2 rose above 1000 ppm, R4 opened the window, and CO2 is still above 1000 ppm at 07:30.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The window closes while CO2 is still high, so stale air stays in the bedroom; R4 won't reopen it until CO2 drops and rises again.
conflicts.explanation: R3's scheduled close reverses R4's open command while the reason for opening still applies.

conflicts.situation: Any time motion is detected on the driveway and R1 turns the halogen floodlight on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The floodlight never switches off. It stays on until something cuts its power, which wastes energy and lights the driveway all the time.
conflicts.explanation: The hot halogen housing sits right above the PIR sensor and keeps motion_drive reporting true. The motion_drive == False trigger of R2 never happens, so R2 can never turn the floodlight off.

conflicts.situation: Earlier driveway motion (for example in the evening while home_mode = home) turned the floodlight on. Later the home switches to night or away mode and an intruder walks onto the driveway.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The driveway camera does not start recording when the intruder arrives, so the security recording is lost.
conflicts.explanation: While the floodlight is lit, its heat keeps motion_drive stuck at true. Real new motion causes no False-to-True change, so R3's trigger never fires again while the mode is night or away.

conflicts.situation: After 23:00, once R5 has switched relay_outdoor off, motion is detected on the driveway at night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 tries to turn on the floodlight, but it stays dark because its circuit has no power. The driveway has no security lighting overnight.
conflicts.explanation: The floodlight is wired to the outdoor lighting circuit that R5 cuts. No rule switches the relay back on, so R1's action has no effect.

conflicts.situation: At 19:00 on every day after R5 first ran at 23:00. No rule ever switches relay_outdoor back on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garden lights stay off even though R4 orders them on. After the first night, the evening garden lighting stops working for good.
conflicts.explanation: The garden lights are powered from the outdoor lighting circuit. R5 turns that relay off, and no rule restores it, so R4's command to the lights' own switch does nothing.

conflicts.situation: A sunny, windy day: lux_balcony > 50000 while wind_speed > 40 km/h. Each time one sensor crosses its threshold again, its rule fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The awning switches back and forth between extended and retracted. If R1 fires after R2, the awning stays extended in strong wind, which the manufacturer forbids and which can damage it.
conflicts.explanation: R1 extends the awning in bright sun and R2 retracts it in strong wind. Both can be true at the same time, so the rules send opposite commands to awning.position.

conflicts.situation: A storm with rain (raining == True) and wind above 40 km/h.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Rain extends the awning during strong wind, or overrides the safety retraction, so the awning risks storm damage.
conflicts.explanation: R3 extends the awning whenever rain is detected, and R2 retracts it in strong wind. Rain and strong wind often come together, so the awning gets opposite commands.

conflicts.situation: Water is detected on the basement floor (sump pump turned on by R1) while home_power exceeds 6000 W.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 switches off the basement relay, which cuts power to the sump pump (and the chest freezer). The pump stops while there is water, so the basement can flood.
conflicts.explanation: The sump pump is plugged into the basement circuit. Load shedding by R3 removes its power, which overrides R1 without being stated in either rule.

conflicts.situation: At 02:00 R4 turns on the washing machine. Its 2.5 kW heating element pushes home_power above 6000 W.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 sheds load by switching off the basement circuit. The chest freezer and sump pump lose power, and no rule turns the circuit back on, so food can spoil and there is no flood protection.
conflicts.explanation: R4's action raises home_power, which triggers R3 without anyone intending it. R3 then cuts the basement circuit's critical loads.

conflicts.situation: After 23:30, when R1 has switched off the TV and AV receiver, someone opens the balcony door.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 powers the AV receiver back on, and HDMI-CEC wakes the TV. The TV turns on late at night against the intent of R1.
conflicts.explanation: R2 only targets the receiver for balcony music, but because of the CEC link the receiver also powers the TV on, which undoes R1's shutdown.

conflicts.situation: At 19:00, R3 switches on the floor lamp, which shines directly on the bookshelf multisensor.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: lux_living rises above 200, so R7 turns the lamp off right away. The scheduled evening light does not stay on.
conflicts.explanation: The lamp's own light raises the illuminance reading and triggers R7, which cancels R3's action.

conflicts.situation: Motion is detected in the living room while lux_living < 30, so R6 turns on the floor lamp.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The lamp raises the sensor's lux reading above 200, R7 turns it off, the room goes dark again, and further motion turns it back on. The lamp flickers on and off.
conflicts.explanation: The lamp sits next to the light sensor, so turning it on triggers R7's brightness threshold, which turns it off again.

conflicts.situation: At 06:30 R1 turns on the steam shower generator; steam drifts from the bathroom onto the landing and the photoelectric detector reads it as smoke (smoke_landing == True).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 fires on a false fire alarm: the siren sounds early in the morning and the house-wide air handler is shut off with no real fire, and it may stay off.
conflicts.explanation: R1's steam changes the smoke reading that R2 watches, so R2 fires when it shouldn't. This is a false alarm caused by another rule's action.

conflicts.situation: Between 22:00 and 08:00 the pool pump is off (R1). The pool water cools below 26 C, so R2 fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns the heater on, but with no water flowing the flow switch keeps the burner off. The pool doesn't get heated overnight, and R2 shows the heater as on even though it isn't heating.
conflicts.explanation: The gas heater's flow switch needs the pump to be running. R1 cuts the pump, which silently cancels what R2 is trying to do.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode, so R7 has turned the heater off, and the pool water drops below 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns the heater back on while the household is away. This undoes R7 and burns gas heating an empty home's pool.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set pool_heater.heating, to on and to off. R2 has no condition on home_mode, so it can fire during away mode.

conflicts.situation: Everyone leaves between 22:00 and 02:00; R1 sets hub.mode to away, then motion_living goes False because nobody is home and R2 sets hub.mode to night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The empty home ends up in night mode instead of away; thermostat goes to 19 C instead of 16 C.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R2 write incompatible values to hub.mode and R2 has no presence condition, so leaving late in the evening causes R2 to override away mode.

conflicts.situation: Departure between 22:00 and 02:00: away mode starts camera recording (via R6), then R2 switches to night mode and R7 stops recording.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room camera stops recording while the home is empty, losing security surveillance.
conflicts.explanation: R2's night-mode switch, triggered by the absence of motion after everyone left, causes R7 to turn off the recording that away mode had started.

conflicts.situation: Morning: R2 turns the radiator on at 06:45, then R1 opens the bedroom window at 07:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The radiator's open-window detection shuts the valve, so the morning heating stops and the bedroom cools instead of warming.
conflicts.explanation: Opening the window makes the radiator thermostat sense a temperature drop and turn the heating off. This undoes R2 without any rule ever turning the heating off.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 goes above 1000 ppm while the radiator is heating (for example after R2 runs at 06:45).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heating stops unexpectedly and the bedroom gets cold.
conflicts.explanation: R4 opens the window, and the radiator thermostat's open-window detection then turns the heating off.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 is above 1000 ppm and outdoor PM2.5 is above 35 at the same time.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The window flips between open and closed. Either polluted outdoor air comes in while the purifier runs, or the room stays at high CO2.
conflicts.explanation: R4 sets the window to open and R5 sets it to closed under conditions that can both be true at once.

conflicts.situation: Outdoor PM2.5 is above 35 at 07:00, after R5 has closed the window and turned on the purifier.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 opens the window anyway, letting polluted air in and working against the purifier.
conflicts.explanation: R1's fixed-time open command overrides R5's pollution-based close command because R1 checks no conditions.

conflicts.situation: Bedroom CO2 is still above 1000 ppm at 07:30, with the window open for ventilation.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 closes the window while CO2 is still high, and CO2 keeps rising without the window reopening.
conflicts.explanation: R3 closes the window on schedule regardless of CO2. R4 only fires when CO2 crosses the threshold, so it does not reopen the window.

conflicts.situation: Any time motion is detected on the driveway and R1 turns the halogen floodlight on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The floodlight stays on indefinitely because R2 never fires. This wastes energy and keeps motion reported on the driveway.
conflicts.explanation: The hot halogen housing above the motion sensor keeps motion_drive true while the floodlight is on. The 'motion stopped' trigger R2 needs never occurs, so R1's action blocks R2.

conflicts.situation: At 23:00 R5 switches relay_outdoor off. No rule switches it back on, so at 19:00 the next day R4 turns garden_lights on while the circuit is still off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: From the second evening on, the garden lights stay dark even though R4 has switched them on.
conflicts.explanation: The garden lights are wired to the outdoor lighting circuit. R5 cuts that circuit permanently, so R4's switch command has no effect.

conflicts.situation: After 23:00 (and on later days while the relay stays off), motion is detected on the driveway, typically in night mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The security floodlight does not come on, so the driveway stays dark and the camera (R3) records unlit footage.
conflicts.explanation: The floodlight is powered by the outdoor lighting circuit that R5 switched off. R1's power-on command can't light the lamp without power.

conflicts.situation: A sunny, windy day: lux_balcony > 50000 while wind_speed > 40 km/h.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The awning gets contradictory commands (extend vs. retract). If R1 fires after R2, or fires again as the light changes, the awning is extended in wind above 40 km/h, which breaks the manufacturer's limit and can damage it.
conflicts.explanation: R1 extends the awning in bright light and R2 retracts it in strong wind. Both triggers can be true at the same time and neither rule checks the other's condition.

conflicts.situation: A rainstorm: raining == True while wind_speed > 40 km/h.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 extends the awning while R2 retracts it. The final position depends on which rule fires last, so the awning can end up extended in storm-force wind and be damaged.
conflicts.explanation: Rain and strong wind often happen together. R3 sets the awning to extended and R2 sets it to retracted, with no rule deciding which one wins.
